items.title: China has sent the world a reminder of its growing military power
items.description: This latest military test demonstrates China's growing willingness to use its military strength to send a warning to the Pacific: that Beijing now has the military and nuclear means to assert its dominance in the region.

items.title: Breaking: Foxtel boss says Kayo 'very well priced' as $5.3b NRL rights deal revealed
items.description: The NRL reveals its new broadcast rights deal worth billions of dollars over seven years from the end of the 2027 season.

items.title: Live: Nine shares up as it retains NRL free-to-air rights for $145m a year
items.description: Nine Entertainment retains the free-to-air rights to the National Rugby League through to 2034. Shares in WiseTech global are surging in early trade.  Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Quick hits: American dream comes crashing down, Mbappé hits back at abuse
items.description: The US goes crashing out of its own World Cup after days of controversy and rancour, while Kylian Mbappé refuses to stand for dreadful racist abuse. Here are today's quick hits.

items.title: TikTok says 98pc of harmful content removed before being seen in Australia
items.description: Most of the harmful content uploaded to TikTok is automatically removed before it can be seen by Australian social media users, the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion hears.

items.title: Microsoft workers in Australia to be caught up in 4,800 global job cuts
items.description: ABC News understands Microsoft Australia staff will be impacted by the tech giant's latest round of lay-offs. Microsoft will cut about 2.1 per cent of its global workforce.

items.title: After months of Trump threats, Cuba says he's committing 'genocide'
items.description: The lives of ordinary Cubans have ground to a halt under an economic and humanitarian crisis that has developed over years and been aggravated by US President Donald Trump's harsh restrictions, experts say.

items.title: Richard White resigns as WiseTech chair but will remain with firm
items.description: The billionaire founder of WiseTech Global said he was stepping down as the company's chair after "recent personal media attention" created an "unnecessary distraction" from the business.

items.title: Pam the Bird graffiti vandal detained after bridge standoff
items.description: A trespasser has been detained by police after spending many hours at the top of a 140- metre-high tower of the Bolte Bridge in Melbourne where he'd spray-painted the surface with the notorious graffiti symbol.

items.title: AFL legend Tony Modra 'overwhelmed by the kindness' after truck crash
items.description: Adelaide Crows legend Tony Modra says he has left hospital after he was seriously injured in a truck crash last month.

items.title: Origin legacies and futures on the line for NSW in decider
items.description: As New South Wales look to rise from the ashes and pull off a Lang Park Origin heist, the future of the team and the legacy of some of its greatest players will be tested in the furnace of a decider.

items.title: Jai Arrow marries partner months after MND diagnosis
items.description: The former Rabbitohs and Queensland NRL player has married his partner Berina Colakovic in a small ceremony in Sydney, months after revealing his motor neurone disease diagnosis.

items.title: Families told accused Bali bomber Hambali to face 202 life terms
items.description: US military prosecutors reveal new details about their case against the man accused of planning the 2002 Bali bombings, telling the loved ones of Australian victims his trial could finally begin next year.

items.title: Government commits to fix dam that 'cannot be repaired'
items.description: The Queensland government announces a plan to rebuild the Paradise Dam wall where it is, despite its operator previously saying there were too many issues to fix it.

items.title: Sick of paying for streaming services? These films and TV series are free
items.description: From Bluey in Yolŋu Matha to the first feature film directed by an Indigenous woman, there is a trove of free movies and TV to dive into this NAIDOC Week.

items.title: What you need to know before claiming your phone as a tax deduction
items.description: The cost of buying and using your own phone may be tax deductible, but the ATO has specific rules about how employees calculate these expenses.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Your challenge in today's ABC Places quiz is to work out the location of 10 photos from around the world. Be warned: we might try to trick you.

items.title: 'Disappointing': Prince Harry and king's awkward stand-off over palace
items.description: The strained relationship between Prince Harry and his father, King Charles III, has been laid bare once again, after an awkward stand-off over accommodation at Buckingham Palace.

items.title: Boys major victims of AI-assisted online sexual abuse, study finds
items.description: About one in every 25 Australians under the age of 18 has been the victim or knows a victim of artificial intelligence-assisted online sexual abuse, according to a new study.

items.title: ADFA cadet facing 79 extra charges after hidden camera found in bathroom
items.description: Police allege Tain Stephens was living at the Australian Defence Force Academy in Canberra when he hid a camera inside a soap dispenser in a female bathroom to capture intimate recordings of women.

items.title: Ex-champion boxer charged over four kidnappings
items.description: Robbery and Serious Crime Squad detectives have charged 26-year-old Humzah Khalid, previously known by his boxing name The Raging Bull, for his alleged involvement in four kidnappings over 10 months.

items.title: 'Incredibly vulnerable' industry becomes new target for scammers
items.description: Amidst a growing number of people taking up gig work to cope with high living costs, scammers are stealing the earnings of "already struggling" delivery drivers.

items.title: 'A lot of stigma': The 'taboo' cancer side effects we don't talk about
items.description: Shame and stigma mean gynaecological side effects from cancer treatment — affecting women's sexual, urinary and reproductive health — are under-reported and under-researched.

items.title: Mushroom murder trial judge shares story in podcast
items.description: Retired judge Christopher Beale has reflected on his long legal career, his temporary pivot to becoming a Jesuit priest and the role he played in the Erin Patterson murder trial.

items.title: Democrats' Platner accused of sexual assault, dashing party's US Senate hopes
items.description: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner says the allegation is "categorically false", but is considering his next steps as the report prompts several key backers to withdraw their endorsements.
